title: Good-morning and wind-down inactivity nudges
description:
The inactivity nudge counted sleep as stillness, so it fired first thing in the morning and again at bedtime saying 'it's been a little while since you moved'. The phone had no quiet hours at all, so an overnight spell fired a minute after the phone was picked up, even at 1am or 6:45am. Now the phone holds any nudge due between 9pm and 8am until 8:00, matching the server's existing quiet window, and the wording follows the local time it fires at: 'Good morning ☀️' from 8 to 11am, 'Stretch your legs?' through the day, 'Winding down 🌙' from 7 to 9pm. The server push picks the same wording per user from their own local hour (it used to build one payload for the whole scan), and both sides pin the strings word for word so the local and server paths read identically.

Also cleared the project's audit backlog so the full check passes. The four iOS-only classes (HealthKitDataSource, MovementActivityMonitor, MovementReminderScheduler, StravaService) had real logic that no test could reach; that logic now lives in static helpers outside the iOS-only blocks with 23 new macOS tests, each proven red by fault injection. 109 unregistered entities were added to the glossary, and generated .build runner files were skip-listed. All 165 scenario screenshots were recaptured after a capture-pipeline update marked them stale: 69 came back pixel-identical, and every changed frame was reviewed against a backup. Several committed frames turned out to be wrong (two iOS home screens, two wrong screens, leaked themes, outdated layouts) and are now correct. Added a scenario-only rbTodayScroll seed (like rbSettingsScroll) so the journal check-in scenario shows its card below the new 'Buddy's read on today' header, and made RaceImportNoKey and RaceImportScaffold internal with their own component scenarios.

Open question left for review: 'Today — Past Race Banner Returns' no longer shows the race banner even with a past race and an eligibility date seeded; the old frame only showed it via leaked state, so this may be a real app bug.
